market_snapshot.breadth_notes: ~9:00 AM PT, third hour of the session: Dow +0.9% (+475 pts, led by Nike, UnitedHealth, Salesforce), S&P 500 turned +0.1% green, Nasdaq pared its loss to -0.4% after falling 1.2% at the open. NYSE advancers better than 2:1 over decliners; slight edge to advancers on Nasdaq (IBD). S&P 500 tech sector down ~1.8% in morning trade, on pace for a ~5.2% weekly loss (MarketWatch/FactSet); chip index on pace for an eighth straight down day while defensives absorb the rotation.
market_snapshot.notes: Thursday Oct 15, ~9:00 AM PT (noon ET). Dip-buying showed up in defensives at midday but the AI selloff kept rolling. September PPI (+1.3% MoM, 6.3% YoY, hottest in 4+ years) still failed to lift the 10Y, which fell ~13 bps from Wednesday's close to 5.06% on the haven bid (IBD). Retail sales +0.8% (double estimates), jobless claims 199K. CME Oct 27-28 hike odds fell to 27% (from 37% post-CPI); December ~90%. CoreWeave CDS blew past 1,000 bps early Thursday (Reuters). VIX morning reading 16.87.

headlines.headline: The midday tape improved: Dow +0.9% (+475 pts, led by Nike, UnitedHealth and Salesforce), S&P 500 turned +0.1% green, Nasdaq pared its loss to -0.4% after opening down 1.2% - dip-buying appeared in defensives while AI-linked names kept selling.
headlines.why_it_matters: The split tape is resolving upward but the leadership is all defensive - the rotation is intact, not reversed, so breadth says caution while the index tape says stabilization.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave's CDS blew out past 1,000 bps early Thursday, from 600 bps Wednesday (Reuters), while CEO Mike Intrator's internal 'irrational' memo and co-founder Brannin McBee's FT interview touting a bid for an investment-grade rating failed to stop the slide; shares fell another ~8%, with longer-dated bond yields near 15%.
headlines.why_it_matters: CDS past 1,000 bps is real default pricing, not equity nerves - and the investment-grade bid is an admission that funding, not demand, is the binding constraint; if credit keeps deteriorating, the equity has no floor.

headlines.headline: Nvidia fell 2.2% in late-morning trade, the biggest drag on the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (-0.5%), after breaching its 50-day line Wednesday; shares are now down ~10% from the record high earlier this month.
headlines.why_it_matters: NVDA is the tape's anchor tenant - its slide below the 50-day while the S&P holds green means the rotation out of AI leverage, not the economy, is still the dominant force.

headlines.headline: Chip stocks are on pace for an eighth straight down day: memory names (Micron, Sandisk, SK Hynix, Seagate, Western Digital) fell 5%+, chip-equipment makers Lam Research and Applied Materials each dropped ~5%, and Intel fell 4%+ below its 50-day - the SOX has erased ~$1.6T in market value over six sessions.
headlines.why_it_matters: Eight straight days with no bounce through TSMC's record print says AI financing, not AI demand, is the sorting variable - and the equipment leg extends the stress from cloud balance sheets into future capex.

headlines.headline: Tesla fell ~2% in late-morning trade ahead of tonight's Roadster demo (5:55pm PT) and Q3 earnings Oct 21; Amazon slipped toward a fourth straight down session; Meta fell ~1% on Guggenheim's $225B 2027 capex estimate - while Apple, Alphabet and Microsoft traded in the green.
headlines.why_it_matters: Megacaps are sorting by capex-and-event overhang: names with spending questions keep selling while the cleaner ones absorb the rotation; Tesla's demo tonight is the next binary.

headlines.headline: September PPI came in at +1.3% MoM (est. 0.6%) and 6.3% YoY (est. 5.5%, hottest since 2022); core PPI +0.7% MoM, 5.0% YoY. Retail sales rose 0.8% (double estimates); jobless claims were 199K. Yet the 10Y fell ~13 bps to 5.06%, and CME Oct 27-28 hike odds fell to 27% from 37% post-CPI.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hottest wholesale inflation print in four-plus years moved hike odds down, not up - the haven bid into Treasuries is doing the market's tightening work, which is classic risk-off and keeps the Oct 28 decision squarely in play.

headlines.headline: Fresh single-name movers: FMC plunged 27% after cutting its Q3 outlook; Penske Automotive rose 8% on a $212/share cash take-private deal; Kimberly-Clark climbed 3% on Q3 prelim sales meeting estimates; Paycom broke out +2%; Williams-Sonoma rallied 3%; Rocket Lab fell 12% (Neutron delayed to 2027); Charles Schwab and PNC fell 3% and 2% on earnings.
headlines.why_it_matters: The one-day movers are all idiosyncratic - guidance cuts, deals, breakouts - a healthy sign that stock-picking still works underneath the macro tape.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried forward: Oct 1 8-K - issued 34.47M Class A units at $26.7206 (fixed 9.25% distribution, non-convertible, non-redeemable, unlisted) to J-W Energy in an internal reorg; began TXSE listing Oct 5 under USAC; Q2 2026 beat Aug 4 ($0.31 EPS vs $0.28 est, $342.15M revenue vs $340.49M est); $600M 6.75% notes due 2035 issued in September to repay credit facility debt; consensus Hold, $29.50 target; units broke below the 200-day MA ($26.92) Oct 13, last ~$25.66.

analysis: What changed vs the 8am brief: (1) the midday tape improved - S&P turned green (+0.1%), Nasdaq pared to -0.4%, Dow extended to +0.9% - as dip-buying showed up in defensives (Nike, UnitedHealth, Salesforce), but the rotation is intact, not reversed: the MAGS ETF still fell 0.5% with NVDA (-2.2%) the biggest drag. (2) Credit stress intensified: CoreWeave CDS blew past 1,000 bps early Thursday from 600 on Wednesday - bond markets are now pricing real default risk, and the co-founder's FT interview about seeking an investment-grade rating is an admission that funding is the binding constraint, not demand. (3) The Fed corner tightened in reverse: the hottest PPI in 4+ years moved October hike odds down to 27% (from 37%) because the haven bid into the 10Y (-13 bps to 5.06%) is doing the tightening work - classic risk-off. (4) Day 8 of the chip rout extended into equipment (LRCX, AMAT -5% each) and Intel (-4%, below its 50-day), spreading the stress from cloud balance sheets to future capex. Signal vs noise: the CRWV CDS blowout and the haven bid are the dominant signal; the Apple/OpenAI trade-secret spat and the one-day single-name movers (FMC, PAG) are contained noise.
